function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning:
The user typed "time". They might want to know the current time? Or they might want to run the time command? In Windows, there's no 'time' command that prints the current time; you can use 'echo %time%' or 'powershell -Command Get-Date'. But the user just typed "time". We need to interpret what they want. Possibly they want to get the current time. So we should respond with the current time. Alternatively, maybe they want to run the 'time' command. But the tool only supports executing commands via cmd_controller_execute. We could call 'time' command, but it will prompt for input. That would hang. So better to provide the current time.

Thus we should output the current time. Let's format as HH:MM:SS. Use UTC or local? Probably local. We'll give local time.
